Report Details

Violation ID: 8209245
Permit API: 113-20470
Unconventional: Yes

Comments: Arrived onsite for a follow up to inspection 3866602 from 11/12/24 that was conducted in response to a release of produced fluid.The affected area near the wells was excavated and was left open to remove any additional fluid that may collect and to facilitate possible excavation or screening as part of Act 2 remediation.At the time of this inspection, there was some water in the pit that had a conductivity of 5.64 milliesiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). The soil conductivity within the pit had a conductivity reading of 0.33 mS/cm. There was some mud near the stockpiled material removed from the pit that had a conductivity of 2.11 mS/cm. This was discussed over the phone with Danielle Schaad, CHK, who already had a vac truck regularly scheduled to remove any accumulating water from the pit. The mud near the stockpiled material was also removed shortly after our phone call.The PCSM and surrounding areas of the pad were screened for soil conductivity. The readings were all between 0.06 mS/cm to 0.27 mS/cm. There were no seeps, puddles, or stressed vegetation observed.There are no new violations noted, however there are outstanding violations against the 23HC well for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, 78a56(a), and OGA3218.2(A) from inspection 3866602 conducted on 11/12/24. There are also outstanding violations against the 104HC from inspection 3835806 conducted on 9/23/24.

CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Inflection Energy (Pa) Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-09-26
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 863612
Permit API: 081-21656
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Eldred Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-09-26
Comments: On September 26, 2019, Department representative Brad Kline conducted an incident investigation at Inflection Energy Winter Well Pad. The Department received notice that Inflection was planning on plugging the conductor of the 3H well. When Inflection entered the bore they found a viscous substance in the bore. The substance is suspected to be synthetic oil based drilling fluid. They pumped out the fluid on 9/24/19. According to Inflection, the conductor is cased 80' down with a depth of 100'. The conductor for the 3H well was drilled in February 2017 along with 3 adjacent wells drilled May through September 2017. The 3 adjacent wells were put into production in 2018. The Department investigated around the conductor and there was no apparent staining on the pad or puddles on the pad. The Department then walked the downgrade slope of the pad and noticed a different shade of soil on the edge of the infiltration berm. A soil sample was collected at that site and sent to be analyzed for Oil and Grease and TPH. Lab results are pending. Inflection continues to investigate the source of the fluid. The release of a regulated substance into the Winter 3H conductor is in violation of the Clean Streams Law 402 (b), Chapter 78a.56a, Section 301 of the Solid Waste Management Act. The Department requests Inflection submit a plan of the actions they will take to address the release and to characterize the extent of the pollution in accordance with Chapter 78a.66(c). The Department recommends proceeding in accordance with Act 2 remediation.

Comments: On April 2, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up Inspection of the RWS Development 001 Well in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. Comments: 08/09/2023This administrative inspection is being conducted for the Ironman Well Site following violations issued on 07/18/2023 (IR: 3589336, Enf: 418538).Violations of 78a57(a), 78a66(b)1ii, 78a66(b)1i, 78a66(b)2, 91.33(A), 91.34(A), 78a54, and SWMA 301 were issued on 07/18/2023, following an incident inspection conducted in response to a spill report recieved by the Department on 07/17/2023. The following is required to be included within the 15 day report, however deficiencies were noted within, specifically A, D, E, and G: 78a.66. Reporting and remediating spills and releases. (c)(2)(i) Within 15 business days of the spill or release, the operator or other responsible party shall provide an initial written report that includes, to the extent that the information is available, the following:(A) The regulated substance involved.(B) The location where the spill or release occurred.(C) The environmental media affected.(D) Pollution or threatened pollution of water supplies.(E) Impacts to buildings or utilities.(F) Interim remedial actions planned, initiated or completed.(G) A summary of the actions the operator or other responsible partyintends to take at the site to address the spill or release such as a schedulefor site characterization, to the extent known, and the anticipated timeframes within which it expects to take those actions.The following deficiencies were noted within the 15 Day Report submitted on 08/02/2023:(A) The regulated substance involved: EQT's report mentions leak from dump line, but does not specifically mention the regulated substance.(C) EQT's report did not mention an assessment of potential impact to Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC).(D) Pollution or threatened pollution of water supplies: Not mentioned in EQT's report.(E) Impacts to buildings or utilities: Not mentioned in EQT's report.(G) A summary of the actions the operator or other responsible party intends to take at the site to address the spill or release such as a schedule for site characterization, to the extent known, and the anticipated time frames within which it expects to take those actions: EQT mentions entering Act 2, but provides no timeline. EQT indicates assessment will focus on dump line trench and northern pad slope, but does not discuss WOC.Due to the deficiencies noted within the 15 Day Report, a violation of 78a66(c)2i is being issued for the failure to provide a complete initial written report within 15 days. Violations issued on 07/18/2023 remain outstanding.

Comments: On April 2, 2024, inspection conducted Brownlee Kelley 12333 well pad in Hopewell Township, Washington County. This inspection follows up to IR 3737318, which was conducted in response to a spill that occurred the day prior. Notice of Termination was approved for this site on August 6, 2021.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Heavy sedimentation was observed in the access road, with accelerated erosion rills observed in the access road closer to the well pad (see photos 2 and 3). However, the Department did not observe it entering off-site Waters of the Commonwealth. Flowback equipment and related secondary containment was removed from site, as well as the rolloff dumpsters containing the impacted material (see photo 4). Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 5). All other machinery and primary containments that appear to contain regulated substances were placed within secondary containment. GPU units onsite were either placed within secondary containment or equipped with interconnected vertical separators (see photo 6). The area formerly impacted by the spill documented in IR 3737318 and IR 3736812 was freshly backfilled with no elevated conductivity detected (see photos 7-10). The ERP was onsite (see photo 10). Well 4H was equipped with a well tag and appeared to be in production (see photos 13 and 14). There are eight other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 12).Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the operator conduct immediate repairs to the access road in a manner that abates the aforementioned accelerated erosion and heavy sedimentation, and prevents it from worsening. Violations issued under IR 3737318 shall remain outstanding, as the NOI to Remediation of the release under Act 2 requirements have not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB Program. Additional violations are being issued against the accelerated erosion and heavy sedimentation observed in the access road.

Comments: On January 3, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection on the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3435475 where violations were outstanding due to a missing Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plans, and no NOV response received from the operator. Also, no production reports had been submitted since 2014 per Department database, at the time of that inspection.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign was present at the well site entrance (see photo 1). No Emergency Response plans, or other required documents were onsite. No evidence of leaks or discharge could be found around the new production tanks, and they appeared to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they were not equipped with secondary containment (see photos 3 and 8). Soil conductivity readings were taken in the earthen berms surrounding these tanks, and at the bases of these tanks (see photos 4-7). The well tag and required operator's information was present on the meter box (see photo 8). The Additional piping and production equipment was left onsite. Some tire rutting was observed at the back of the well site looking from the road, which could be due to third party traversing (see photo 10). The ground overall was soft, which could lead to future stabilization concerns. Therefore, the Department recommends that the operator take additional stabilization measures to prevent any potential E and S issues from developing.Based on observations from today's inspection, the violations that were continued in IR 3435475 shall remain outstanding, since no changes were made since and no NOV response has been received to date. An additional violation shall be issued against the production tanks, since they are not equipped with secondary containment in an unconventional site.

The pit was filled and no elevated conductivity was noted in the area (Photo 15).No stressed vegetation noted and no elevated conductivity within vegetation (Photo 16). Bank was cut for access.A vac truck removed material from the excavated pits and was in a container on site (Photo 17).Additional material labeled was on site (Photos 18, 19).Due to the release of production fluid to to pad, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/13/2020
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 896989
Permit API: 015-23526
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wilmot Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/13/2020
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that approximately 60-70 gallons of diesel spilled to the pad surface. A frac is on-going on this location. Upon arriving on location, I met with company man Josh Lumbardo. He showed me the location of the release which was tarped due to the rain. Mark Patty, HSE for Chesapeake, then arrived. Mr. Patty said that he believed it was an estimated 65 gallons of diesel released from a diesel delivery truck. An estimated 40 gallons of that is believed to have impacted the surface while the remainder was contained on a piece of secondary containment. A portion of pad material was excavated, placed on secondary containment on the pad, and tarped. Mr. Patty said that Creston Environmental was contracted to investigate the release and to take samples from the pad surface. He also stated that diesel was observed leaching out from beneath the rig mats adjacent to the area of the release. Mr. Patty said that the rig mats would likely be removed as soon as the frac was completed, which he estimates will take 10 more days. Then the area beneath the rig mats will be investigated to assess the extent of the impact. Beneath the tarp on the impacted area of the pad, the fluid appeared to have a gray sheen, it felt oily, and had a faint diesel odor. During this inspection, I recommended to Mr. Patty that they install a sump in the impacted area of the pad and remove fluid from the sump and the surrounding area on an as-needed basis.The Department recommends removing as many rig mats as possible adjacent to the impacted pad area as soon as possible, prior to the completion of the frac, to assess the extent of the impact and to remove any material impacted by the release.The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance 78a.66 due to the unknown extent of the impact to the pad surface which undermines the ability to accurately estimate the spill volume.Violations noted.

Comments: Routine field inspection performed in late afternoon with cool, cloudy weather conditions, and 48 degrees. Last inspection performed on 5/25/15, more than 7 years ago. Wellhead is located atop hillside in opening surrounded by partially wooded area of residential setting ~60' South of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility (photo #2). At the wellhead surface casing valve is open, lower left side production tubular valve cracked open to port with valve open to drip/domestic house gas meter run, lower production tubular right side valve is closed, upper production tubular is plumbed with t-shaped union and open valve union, and the production tubular plumbed on right side (opposite meter) of head to sales/surface equipment with open valve; annulus is buried, unable to determine if vented (photos #2, #3, #4, and #5). Meter reading (photo #6). A functioning pressure gauge in-line at meter present, reading ~13 psi at time of inspection (photo #7). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility and does not require a well label/marker. Some trace to occasionally moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility, one 50 bbl poly tank, and one 100 bbl steel tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #8). Valve open on main tubular feeding separator and open valves to and from separator (photo #9). A 31-day production chart is present with recordings and dated 10/31/22 (photo #10). Well posting signage affixed to steel tank with all information about well and current Operator present, except the Operator contact address information (photo #11). Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment and tank. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add contact address information to the permanent well posting signage affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, 2019, and 2018. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2017 stating 53 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 0 Mcf recorded over 365 days. The 2021 annual production report submitted indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 or blank production values under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021 and 2020 production reports. The last reported production value was in 2019 of 6 Mcf recorded over 365 days. Wellhead field verified and GPS coordinates of well updated with this inspection showed a moderate distance offset of ~179 ft between coordinates (photo #12). This well appears to be back in production based on this inspection, the chart at facility with recordings, and the open valves with meter at wellhead. This is an active, producing well with a domestic house gas meter at wellhead.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Bull Run Resources Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-06-29
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 887754
Permit API: 083-54017
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Wetmore Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-29
Comments: The operator contacted Brian Ayers to report multiple spills at the Collins Pine 22 well site the morning of 6/29/2020. This inspection was performed as a complaint inspection to CID #350759. The operator was intending to perform an injection test on this well for a proposed injection well permit. They had a 500 barrel laydown tank on location that was filled with brine over the course of several days prior to the test. The operator noted on arriving at the site 6/29 that the site was wet, and then was able to see that the tank was actively leaking brine. They were able to contact a vac truck operator who sent trucks to empty the tank. A mini excavator was used to dig a small trench on the north side of the site. In the interim, the operator hooked a hose from the tank to drain into the well in order to reduce the level of the tank. The packer in the well failed, which allowed oil to be displaced and flow out the backside of the packer string and onto the ground. The operator noticed the discharge and immediately shut the well in and ceased flowing water. They had a mini excavator on site and dug another interceptor trench in the access road to cut off oil from flowing further down gradient toward Route 6. 1-2 barrels of oil was estimated to have been released from this well. At the time of this inspection, the operator had determined that 3" of water had drained from the full tank prior to discovery of the leak, which occurred at approximately 10 am. Further leaking occurred during the time between discovery and the emptying of the tank at approximately 2 PM. The total loss of brine is estimated to be between 5 and 10 barrels. Various areas surrounding the tank were tested with a soil EC meter, which read between 15 mS and >20 mS. Oil was all contained within the trench or puddles on the location, with no threat of further contamination. The operator intends to have a rolloff container on site this evening and begin to scrape up the contaminated soil on site, starting with the area contaminated with crude oil. A vac truck will be on site should extra encountered.

Comments: Incident inspection of Chesapeake's "Rocks" Marcellus shale well site. The ESCGP covers 3 separate Marcellus sites. This inspection only covers "Rocks" (not Dryscoll or Oil Can).Danielle Schaad called the DEP on Monday January 27, 2025 to report an estimated 5 gallon release of produced liquid from a hammer union to the pad surface. The release occurred during flowback operations that day. Some of the liquid flowed under liner containment for GasBuster tanks, so they removed 2 of the Gasbusters and part of the liner on January 28 to be able to excavate impacted material. I spoke with Andy Steffe and Tiffany Smith (both Creston Environmental) on site. During this inspection they collected field screening soil samples from the edges of the excavated area in glass jars and mixed in distilled water to make a slurry. The 16 samples returned electrical conductivity (EC) readings of 0.02-1.65 mS/cm with a YSI meter. Only 1 of the jars returned EC >1.0 mS/cm. A track hoe removed pad material from the spot that was 1.65 mS/cm during this inspection. The removed pad material is placed on liner containment on the SW corner of the pad. Creston will also send soil samples to a lab today to comply with Act 2 Cleanups, since the volume of the release is unknown. They plan on backfilling the excavated area today after sampling.Danielle Schaad messaged that they covered the waste pile with plastic. The excavated area was approximately 43'x32'x2' deep which equals 125 cubic yards; they backfilled it today after my inspection.Violations are cited to the 015-23897 permit.Precision Drilling 573 drilled the 3 new Marcellus wells here on February-March, 2024. Universal hydraulically fractured the 3 new Marcellus wells here in July 2024.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site, but cannot fully assess stabilization because of partial snow cover. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed.I did not see any pooled water on the pad surface, just snow. Moist soil on the pad has electrical conductivity of 0.72 mS/cm with a Hanna Soil Test.Air temp 27FJLP

Comments: I conducted a follow up inspection of this conventional well that had a release occur in November of 2025, when a steel gathering line had ruptured resulting in crude oil contaminating ditches and soil. Initially the remediation of the site was progressing. There had been no signs of product at the under flow dams, there was no viable oil in the ditches. In preperation of obtaining confirmatory soil samples to evaluate if the remediation was sufficient, it was discovered another leak had developed on a different section of the same line. This operator indicated they will replace all of the steel line for this well with plastic/poly line. This release was caught early and as of now, appears to be less than 1 bbl of lost product and has impacted a minimal amount of soil.Bull Run employees had a roll off dumpster en-route to remove the impacted soil. The ruptured line was sucked out with a vac truck and will be removed while running new poly line. Further inspections will be conducted to document ongoing remedation efforts, as well as confirmatory sampling to show that the remediation is sufficient.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 9/21/2026
Comments: On September 21, 2026, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response site inspection at the EQT ARO LLC COP Tract 027B Pad B. EQT reported to the DEP spill hotline that a water truck hauling produced fluid spilled approximately 100 gallons of produced fluid from a faulty sight glass on the water truck onto the access road of the well pad at 0800. Upon arriving onsite, EQT had delineated the spill on the access road and had that area blocked off from traffic. EQT said that Penn E and R was responding to assist with the investigation and collect confirmatory samples for the ACT 2 process. EQT was investigating how much of the produce fluid had spilled off the road edge. Approximately three areas along the road edge were found to have elevated soil conductivity. One of the areas found was a culvert with produced fluid caught in the outfall. The soil conductivity of the impacted area ranged from 200 uS/cm to over 4,000 uS/cm, which is the upper limit of the DEP soil conductivity meter. The delineated area of impact was approximately 10 feet by 415 feet measure by Penn E and R. While onsite, equipment was delivered to begin the excavation of the impacted area. EQT's contractor began removing the impacted soil from the access road. The contractor scraped the road surface and excavated approximately 4-6 inches of soil off the road edge to removed the impacted soil. Approximately 100 feet of the spill area had been excavated prior to DEP leaving the site. Violations of the Clean Streams Law 401, Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted. EQT plans to remediate the spill through the ACT 2 process.

Comments: On May 21, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up inspection of Apollo Resource's Whyel 1 Well located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following violations issued under inspection report 3875658. No NOV response has been received regarding the violations previously issued.At the time of this inspection a well posting was observed on a production tank with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from the production tank.At the time of this inspection, the Department did not observe any active fluid leaks or discharges from the annulus which is the location of the previously observed dripping/leaking, this annulus also appears to have been repaired.Conductivity readings were taken in the area below the annulus (0.1613 mS, 0.0511 mS, and 0.220 mS) and were compared to a background soil conductivity reading taken in some vegetation adjacent to the well site (0.1369 mS). These soil conductivity readings are comparable to the background soil conductivity reading, however, the Operator has yet to provide the Department with the following:-A written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, and remediation actions for the spill or release. -The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. -The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding pending the receipt of the aforementioned documents.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-12-05 to Chevron Appalachia Llc in South Huntingdon Twp, Westmoreland county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Chevron Appalachia Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-12-05
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 870822
Permit API: 129-28979
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: South Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-12-05
Comments: The inspection is being conducted in response to a spill reported by Chevron on 12/5/2019 at 10:30AM. According to the initial spill report, greater than 5 gallons of oil-based drilling mud was found under secondary containment upon removal of said containment. Removal of secondary containment is currently underway at the time of inspection. Chevron representative Curtis Small is on site. The Act 9 sign is present at the site entrance. The ERP, PPC, ESCGP approval, site plans, and drill permits are in the mailbox. No inspection logs or worksheets are present on site. Secondary containment inspections and repair records were requested from Curtis Small; he stated that the logs were not on site. Drilling mud and staining is present in multiple locations on the well pad (Photos #6, 7, 8, and 10) evidencing multiple breaches of secondary containment in multiple locations on the pad thereby strongly suggesting the drilling mud spill was substantial and widespread. Drilling mud has mixed with stormwater and has collected in puddles over greater than half the pad area (Photos # 9, 11, and 13). Multiple water puddles have a strong petroleum odor and have a greasy consistency, especially the dark areas at puddle edges (Photos #11 and 13). The contaminated stormwater has likely left the pad in multiple places and entered stormwater features and diversion channels. An unknown quantity of material has also been spilled near the pad entrance (Photos #2 and 3). Individual material particles are readily visible with the naked eye, coarse, and appear to be predominately silica. The Department requests the information on the material. The SW corner of the pad contains significant quantities of sediment and tire ruts (Photos #4 and 5). Multiple pieces of equipment currently not in use and lacking secondary containment are scattered around the well pad (Photos #1, 11, 12, and 13).
